# REMAINING WORK — Geelooy Movie and Studio Unification

The Awtsmoos renews each frame before the frame can claim its name;
Awtsmoos.com must hold one movie heart, while every studio keeps its flame.

## Evidence already established
- [x] Real repository root inspected at `work/awtsmoos.com/geelooy`.
- [x] Native tunnel route verified against the user's Mac checkout.
- [x] Existing movie/studio surfaces identified: `animator`, `video-editor`, `mitzvah-studio`, `nesher-studio`.
- [x] Confirmed `apps/awtsmoos-studio` does not currently exist.
- [x] Confirmed `libs/awtsmoos-procedural-core` already contains substantial animation, character, procedural asset, particle, text, camera, geometry, physics, and JSON reality systems.
- [x] Confirmed heavy concurrent work exists; no reset, stash, destructive cleanup, or blind rewrite is permitted.
- [x] Read independent parallel movie-unification plans and preserved their compatible requirements.

## Discovery still required before source writes
- [ ] Read library package/export conventions and public entry points.
- [ ] Read current core animation/assets/particles/text/camera facades used by applications.
- [ ] Read current app entry points and trace imports for animator, video-editor, mitzvah-studio, nesher-studio.
- [ ] Search for existing general JSON-to-DOM/UI frameworks inside `libs/awtsmoos` before creating a new shared UI namespace.
- [ ] Re-check git status and hashes for every legacy file considered for modification.
- [ ] Identify whether another live agent has already landed canonical movie modules or an `awtsmoos-studio` app before our source pass.

## Architecture work
- [ ] Define canonical declarative movie document schema.
- [ ] Define deterministic timeline, scene-local time, interpolation, easing, transition, and camera-cut semantics.
- [ ] Define AI-repairable validation errors with JSON paths and actionable reasons.
- [ ] Define engine-neutral scene vocabulary for actors, people, 2D shapes, 3D primitives, text, diagrams, charts, arrows, callouts, particles, lights, cameras, audio/caption cues, groups, and reusable assets.
- [ ] Bridge canonical assets into existing Awtsmoos Procedural Core generators rather than duplicating generation logic.
- [ ] Define renderer/adaptor contracts so 2D and 3D share timing/meaning but preserve distinct rendering paths.
- [ ] Define studio persona/pet descriptors so each app keeps specialized UX and capabilities.
- [ ] Define general Awtsmoos UI JSON grammar, normalization, event/action binding, responsive tokens, and DOM rendering.

## Implementation work
- [ ] Add canonical movie modules to shared core with small files and explicit exports.
- [ ] Add shared Awtsmoos UI library or extend the correct existing shared UI home if discovery proves one already exists.
- [ ] Add a new mobile-first `apps/awtsmoos-studio` flagship that composes shared movie + UI systems.
- [ ] Add thin compatibility/adaptor modules for existing studio apps without flattening their identity.
- [ ] Reuse/extract only genuinely generic asset generation into Awtsmoos Procedural Core.
- [ ] Keep renderer/media/export-specific code in adapters when it depends on app/runtime capabilities.
- [ ] Provide AI-safe movie compile/validate/repair loop from declarative JSON.
- [ ] Provide mobile-first prompt, preview, scene navigator, timeline, inspector, play/seek, and export controls.

## Three-minute proof movie
- [ ] Build exactly 180 seconds of authored movie data.
- [ ] Use at least 12 scenes with clearly different composition and pacing.
- [ ] Include 2D infographic/tutorial scenes and 3D cinematic scenes.
- [ ] Include multiple characters/people with reusable identities.
- [ ] Include animated text, titles, captions, geometric shapes, arrows, charts, labels, callouts, masks/patches, and panels.
- [ ] Include particle systems and procedural effects.
- [ ] Include at least six camera compositions/angles plus camera motion and hard/soft cuts.
- [ ] Include transitions, easing variety, keyframed transforms, layered groups, and scene-local animation.
- [ ] Include beginning, teaching/progression, conflict/energy rise, climax, recap, and credits-like ending.
- [ ] Make the proof loadable in the flagship app without hidden manual setup.
- [ ] Attempt actual encoded movie export through verified existing export infrastructure; if an environment capability prevents encoding, record the exact boundary rather than claiming success.

## Verification work — only after first full source-writing pass
- [ ] Re-read every touched source file in full.
- [ ] Verify every touched code file uses tabs and stays at or under the user line-size ceiling by splitting modules.
- [ ] Syntax-check every touched JavaScript module.
- [ ] Run relevant existing tests for procedural core and each integrated studio.
- [ ] Add focused tests for canonical movie schema, validation, timeline boundaries, interpolation, renderer contracts, and UI grammar.
- [ ] Assert proof movie duration exactly equals 180 seconds.
- [ ] Assert proof movie feature inventory contains people, text, shapes, infographics, particles, 2D, 3D, cameras, transitions, and animation.
- [ ] Browser-load every affected route.
- [ ] Inspect console/runtime errors.
- [ ] Verify desktop layout.
- [ ] Verify narrow/mobile viewports and touch-friendly controls.
- [ ] Seek representative timestamps throughout the complete movie.
- [ ] Exercise AI JSON editing/import path.
- [ ] Exercise export path and inspect produced artifact if encoding succeeds.

## Closure and shadow work
- [ ] Write planned-vs-actual delta after first implementation pass.
- [ ] Complete a second source-writing pass if any required behavior is missing.
- [ ] Re-read all touched files again after fixes.
- [ ] Compare original three-phase plan against actual implementation.
- [ ] Record limitations, evidence, commands, runtime checks, and artifact paths.
- [ ] Re-scan for unfinished movie/studio duplication and hidden missing integrations.
- [ ] Stop only when every safe in-scope item is completed or tied to a concrete hard capability boundary.
